subject.title: [Bug]: Slack replies ~2s slower than other channels — dominant cost is Socket Mode event delivery; channel-side stalls fixed in #101888

question: Should OpenClaw resolve this issue by documenting HTTP Request URLs as the preferred low-latency hosted Slack transport, or by changing Slack setup/default behavior beyond the existing `mode: "http"` support?
rationale: HTTP mode already exists and the remaining measured delay is mostly before OpenClaw receives the event, but changing recommendation or defaults affects Slack setup expectations and deployment requirements.

options.title: Document HTTP latency guidance
options.body: Keep Socket Mode as the local/private-ingress default and explicitly recommend HTTP Request URLs for hosted public-ingress Slack deployments where reply latency matters.

options.title: Change setup or defaults
options.body: Sponsor a stronger setup/default change that steers new hosted Slack installs away from Socket Mode, with upgrade and operator guidance.

options.title: Accept current guidance
options.body: Decide the existing transport table is sufficient and close only after recording that no latency-specific Slack guidance is planned.

recommendation.title: Document HTTP latency guidance
recommendation.body: Keep Socket Mode as the local/private-ingress default and explicitly recommend HTTP Request URLs for hosted public-ingress Slack deployments where reply latency matters.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the measurement, the current-main partial fix, and the comment scoping the remaining work to HTTP-mode guidance.
